subject: Money
title: Keeping Up with the Joneses
description: One-minute skill: Keeping Up with the Joneses.

hook.text: Your neighbor buys a new car. Suddenly your perfectly fine car feels inadequate. Nothing changed but context.

buildup.text: Social comparison drives spending. We judge our wealth relative to peers, not by absolute standards.

discovery.text: Robert Frank found that spending on visible goods (cars, houses) rises fastest. It's about status display.

twist.text: Social media made the Joneses global. Now you compare to curated lifestyles of millions, not neighbors.

climax.text: You can't win a comparison game with no finish line. Someone always has more.

quiz.question: What kind of goods does social comparison most affect?
